back: Development that meets present needs without reducing the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
Using resources at a rate that allows renewal or replacement, protecting the environment and sharing benefits fairly.
Communal Areas Management Programme for Indigenous Resources.
Communities receive income from wildlife (safari hunting, tourism), so they have a reason to protect animals rather than poach them.

front: Give three roles of the Environmental Management Agency.
back: Requires environmental impact assessments; monitors pollution; enforces rules on waste, veld fires and river-bank cultivation; educates the public.

front: What are community share ownership trusts?
back: Trusts that receive a share of the value or profits of large local resource companies, to spend on community development.

front: Give two benefits and one problem of recycling.
back: Saves raw materials and energy, reduces waste, creates jobs; but collection and sorting are costly.

front: How can a non-renewable resource be used sustainably?
back: Use it efficiently, recycle where possible, and invest the income in education and infrastructure for future generations.

front: Give three lessons from newly industrialised countries.
back: Invest in education and skills; high saving and investment; export-led manufacturing; stable planning; build in environmental protection.
